details: Bitcoin slipped to around $76,900 and Ethereum to $2,290 on April 28-29, influenced by escalating geopolitical tensions, particularly regarding the Strait of Hormuz, which is weighing on overall risk sentiment. Both Bitcoin and Ethereum spot Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) recorded significant outflows; Bitcoin ETFs saw over $263 million in net outflows, and Ethereum ETFs experienced $21.8 million in net outflows on April 28.
title: Bitcoin, Ethereum See Price Dips Amid Geopolitical Concerns and ETF Outflows

details: The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) jointly released guidance that primarily classifies most cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, and XRP, as digital commodities rather than securities. This regulatory clarity, issued last month but reported on April 28, 2026, is anticipated to encourage greater institutional investment in the crypto sector.
title: US Regulators Issue Clarified Crypto Asset Classification

details: Several US states are implementing diverse regulations for virtual currency kiosks. Wisconsin, Virginia, Wyoming, and South Dakota enacted new laws in 2026, while Indiana and Tennessee moved to ban them entirely, citing fraud concerns. These regulations typically cover licensing, fraud warnings, and daily transaction limits, reflecting a growing focus on consumer protection.
title: US States Implement New Crypto ATM Regulations and Bans

details: The decentralized finance (DeFi) sector demonstrated resilience following an April 18, 2026, exploit involving rsETH on the Unichain bridge, which led to 116,500 rsETH being released. Aave and DeFi United initiated recovery efforts, and Standard Chartered reiterated its bullish $2 trillion outlook for the Real World Asset (RWA) market within DeFi, citing the sector's maturity and rapid response to security incidents.
title: DeFi Sector Shows Resilience After $292M Exploit, Standard Chartered Upbeat

details: Robinhood Markets reported a significant decline in its Q1 crypto trading revenues, dropping by 47% year-over-year. This disappointing performance, reported on April 28, 2026, missed analysts' expectations and suggests a cooling in retail crypto trading activity on the popular brokerage platform.
title: Robinhood's Q1 Crypto Revenue Falls by Nearly 50%
